pages.text: Twice a day, the river water dropped, revealing wide sandbanks. Clams hid in the sand.
Bung had already put a basket at the bow. "When the water goes out, Ddori and I will pick clams!"
The water dropped. A wide stretch of sand appeared.
But the awning shade was so cool! Bung lay down. "Later."
Ddori dragged the basket over. Bung rolled over again. "A little longer."
Slowly, the water returned. Little by little, the sand disappeared.
Now water filled everything. Bung's basket was empty.
Grandpa passed with his oar on his shoulder—a long wooden paddle for the boat. "Did the water wait for you?"
Next day, Bung picked up the basket as soon as the water dropped. Mom followed.
Bung and Ddori picked clams one by one. The full basket grew heavy.
